title: The Move-Out Cleaning Checklist That Gets the Deposit Back
metaTitle: Move-Out Cleaning Checklist for Getting Your Deposit Back
metaDescription: The places a walkthrough actually checks: inside the oven, behind the fridge, the range hood filter, door tops, window tracks. Room by room, in order.
summary: A walkthrough grades the places you never clean while you live somewhere, which is why normal cleaning fails it.
transcript: Landlords and property managers don't grade a move-out clean the way you'd grade your own house. They walk a list, and the list is mostly the places nobody cleans while they're living somewhere.
Work empty. Everything out first, including the closets and the garage. A clean done around boxes gets done again.
Then top to bottom, front to back. Ceiling fans, light fixtures and vent covers before anything underneath them. Mop first and you'll mop twice.

The kitchen is where deposits are won and lost. Inside the oven, including the door glass and under the bottom drawer. Inside and underneath the refrigerator, and pull it out, because the walkthrough will. Inside every cabinet and drawer, not just the fronts. Under and behind the range. The range hood filter, which is usually the greasiest thing in the unit and almost always missed.

Bathrooms. Behind and underneath the toilet, including the bolt caps and the floor where the base meets the tile. The exhaust fan cover. Mirror edges. Under the sink, where old leak stains and product rings live. Shower glass and grout have their own tips.

Everywhere else. Every baseboard. Window tracks and sills. The tops of doors, which hold a line of dust at exactly eye level for anyone tall. Switch plates and handles. Closet shelves and rods. Light globes, which usually have insects in them.
Walls get spot cleaned, carefully. Flat paint burnishes when you scrub it, leaving a shiny patch that reads worse than the mark did. Test in a corner first.
Floors last. Vacuum carpet in both directions. If there are pet stains, say so instead of hoping. A disclosed stain is a deduction. A hidden one found later is a deduction plus an argument.
Two things people forget completely. The dryer lint trap and the vent behind it, and the floor of the water heater closet.
Photograph everything when you're finished, in daylight, with the lights on. Timestamped photos of an empty clean unit settle most deposit disputes before they start.
localNote: Most leases here run on a standard walkthrough form, and around NMSU a lot of them turn over inside the same two weeks of July and August. If you're moving in that window, book the clean early, because that's when every cleaner in town is full.

faq.q: Do I have to shampoo the carpet?
faq.a: Read the lease. Plenty of them here require professional carpet cleaning with a receipt, separate from the general clean. Skip it when it's required and they'll have it done and bill you at their rate.

faq.q: How long does a move-out clean take?
faq.a: For an empty two bedroom, most of a day done properly. The oven and the rest of the kitchen are usually two to three hours on their own.

faq.q: Is it cheaper to do it myself?
faq.a: In cash, yes. The real question is whether the walkthrough passes, because a deduction is often bigger than the clean would have cost.

faq.q: What if I've already left town?
faq.a: That's normal on a move-out. The place is empty, so nobody needs to be there as long as we can get access.
